question: What is the nature of the phonemic ground that makes convention possible?
premises: Conventions require a stable, non-regressive ground.
There is an infinite, non-māyic collection of phonemes of this kind.
This phonemic collection is always accompanied by conscious reflective awareness and continually unfolds.
inference: The stable ground of convention is an infinite, non-māyic phonemic totality that perpetually unfolds with conscious reflective awareness.
plain_english: Therefore, this infinite, non-māyic collection of phonemes, accompanied by the reflective awareness of consciousness, is always unfolding.
